Axiom: DbC contracts are textual and language-agnostic. Write preconditions / postconditions / invariants and public operations as plain intent-level statements in the shared vocabulary (Port, Adapter, Entity, Command, Query, Event) — one testable statement per line, readable, free of syntax noise. Concrete signatures and types belong to the execution phase: the coding rules turn the contract into the project's language there. The single exception: Golden DX / usage examples are written in the project's target language — they show consumption, the contract stays textual. A genuinely cross-language contract belongs in an `interface` scope, expressed in its own interface language (schema / proto / IDL), not here.
